description:
## Overview

The SVC_$ subsystem implements Domain/OS syscall dispatching via M68K TRAP instructions.
Each TRAP number corresponds to a different argument count for syscall validation.

## Completed Work

- **TRAP #0** (0 args): `domain_os/svc/sau2/trap0.s` - Simple syscalls, no argument validation
- **TRAP #1** (1 arg): `domain_os/svc/sau2/trap1.s` - Validates USP + 1 arg, 66 entries at 0xe7b05c
- **TRAP #2** (2 args): `domain_os/svc/sau2/trap2.s` - Validates USP + 2 args, 133 entries at 0xe7b094
- **TRAP #3** (3 args): `domain_os/svc/sau2/trap3.s` - Validates USP + 3 args, 155 entries at 0xe7b0d8
- **TRAP #4** (4 args): `domain_os/svc/sau2/trap4.s` - Validates USP + 4 args, 131 entries at 0xe7b120
- **TRAP #5** (5 args): `domain_os/svc/sau2/trap5.s` - Complex syscalls, validates USP + 5 args, 99 entries
- **TRAP #6** - Not used for SVC calls (points to FIM_$UNDEF_TRAP)
- **TRAP #7** (6 args): `domain_os/svc/sau2/trap7.s` - Validates USP + 6 args, 59 entries at 0xe7b1d8
- **TRAP #8** (variable args): `domain_os/svc/sau2/trap8.s` - Variable-argument dispatcher, uses argcount lookup table, 56 entries at 0xe7b240
- **Shared tables**: `domain_os/svc/svc_tables.c` - C code, shared across SAUs
- **Header**: `domain_os/svc/svc.h` - Constants, syscall numbers, table declarations

## TRAP Numbering Note

TRAP #6 is NOT used for SVC dispatching - it points to FIM_$UNDEF_TRAP which generates a fault. The naming convention follows the actual M68K TRAP instruction numbers:
- SVC_$TRAP0-5: Handle M68K TRAP #0-5
- SVC_$TRAP7: Handles M68K TRAP #7 (6-arg syscalls)
- SVC_$TRAP8: Handles M68K TRAP #8 (variable-arg syscalls)

All SVC TRAP dispatchers are now complete.
close_reason: All SVC TRAP dispatchers (0-5, 7-8) implemented. Corrected naming: TRAP #6 is unused, TRAP #7 handles 6-arg syscalls, TRAP #8 handles variable-arg syscalls.

title: smd_cursor_pos_t field order does not match the packed position
description: The kernel carries a cursor position as one longword with X in the LOW half and Y in the HIGH half (proved in smd_$write_str_clip_impl 0x00E703F6: the low half is clipped against +0x56/+0x58 and shifted right by 4 to index words within a scan line, the high half against +0x5A/+0x5C).  In big-endian terms that makes offset 0x00 the Y and 0x02 the X, but smd/smd.h's smd_cursor_pos_t declares {int16_t x; int16_t y}.  smd/smd_internal.h now provides SMD_POS_X/SMD_POS_Y/SMD_POS_MAKE and the hot paths (hw->cursor_pos, SMD_GLOBALS.default_cursor_pos, saved_cursor_pos, smd_event_entry_t.pos) use a plain uint32_t.  smd_cursor_pos_t is still exported to other subsystems (SMD_$DISPLAY_CURSOR, SMD_$SET_UNIT_CURSOR_POS, TPAD_$SET_UNIT_CURSOR), so fixing it needs those callers checked too.
close_reason: smd_cursor_pos_t is now 'typedef uint32_t' - the packed longword the kernel actually manipulates - and SMD_POS_X/SMD_POS_Y/SMD_POS_MAKE moved from smd_internal.h to smd.h so external callers get them too.  This is the endian-safe fix: a {int16_t;int16_t} struct can only be right on one byte order, whereas every SMD entry point loads the position with a single move.l (SMD_$DISPLAY_CURSOR 0x00E6E096, SMD_$CLEAR_CURSOR 0x00E6E0C0, SMD_$SET_TP_CURSOR 0x00E6E976, SMD_$SET_UNIT_CURSOR_POS 0x00E6E7EC) and smd_$write_str_clip_impl 0x00E703F6 takes the LOW half as X and the high half as Y.  All seven in-tree users already cast to uint32_t*, so the casts simply went away; the one cross-subsystem call, TPAD_$SET_UNIT_CURSOR, now takes an explicit (smd_$pos_t *) cast with a comment - tpad/tpad.h's union smd_$pos_t already declares {int16_t y; int16_t x}, which is the m68k memory image of the same value and independent corroboration.  _Static_assert on sizeof == 4.  The same row-first convention was found in smd_hdm_pos_t and fixed there too (see source-nhzy): SMD_$COPY_FONT_TO_HDM 0x00E70328/0x00E70330 uses +0x00 as the scan line and 0x00E70340 uses +0x02 as the column.

title: win: DISK_INIT (0x00e19986) is WIN-internal and has no C file
description:
disk/misc/disk_init.c was removed (bead source-5ky): it was never built, contained an extern FUN_00e190bc reference and a stale EC_$WAIT call, and it does not belong to the disk subsystem.

Evidence: DISK_INIT lives at 0x00e19986, entirely inside the WIN (Winchester driver) code region, and its only callers are WIN_$DINIT (0x00e19d32) and FUN_00e194b4 (0x00e194e0).  Its helper FUN_00e190bc is called from WIN_$ANSI_COMMAND (0x00e1916a), SEEK (0x00e195d8) and DISK_INIT itself.  So the prototype stays in win/win.h; it must NOT move to disk/disk.h.

Work: emit DISK_INIT under win/ (566 bytes, ANSI drive identification for Micropolis 1203 / PRIAM 3450 / PRIAM 7050), identify and rename FUN_00e190bc, and convert its EC_$WAIT call (0xe19..., three eventcounts) to the by-value ec_$wait_ecs_t / ec_$wait_vals_t signature in ec/ec.h.
close_reason: DISK_INIT (0x00E19986, 566 bytes) emitted as win/disk_init.c with win/test/test_disk_init.c (9 tests).  It is WIN-internal: bsr-called with the status in D0 and no Pascal result slot.  Its seven arguments are (unit:w, sub_unit:w, ^total_blocks:long, ^blocks_per_track:word, ^heads:word, ^geometry:word[2], ^drive_id:word); WIN_$DINIT swaps its own first two when it calls it (0x00E19D2C/0x00E19D30).  Ten-attempt retry loop (moveq #9 + dbf, 0x00E199C8/0x00E19AA2), the spin-up branch gated on bit 0 of the general status, and the geometry table for Micropolis 1203 / PRIAM 3450 / PRIAM 7050 including the original's fall-through on an unrecognised id (0x00E19B80 sets the error but still multiplies with D1 holding the drive id, overwriting *total_blocks).  FUN_00e190bc identified and renamed in Ghidra to WAIT_FOR_CONTROLLER: it spins on bit 15 (busy) of the drive status word at regs+6 with a 3-tick TIME_$CLOCKH deadline (status_$disk_controller_busy 0x00080002 on timeout) then maps bit 7 to status_$disk_not_ready; emitted as win/wait_for_controller.c with win/test/test_wait_for_controller.c (5 tests).  The EC_$WAIT at 0x00E19A66 is converted to the by-value ec_$wait_ecs_t / ec_$wait_vals_t form: ecs {&WIN_EC[unit], &TIME_$CLOCKH, NULL}, vals {ec+1, TIME_$CLOCKH+0x78, 0}.  The prototype stayed in win/win.h.

title: TTY: confirm historical names for char classes 0x05/0x06 (XON vs XOFF)
description: tty/tty.h: class 0x05 (0xE1BA42) sets TTY_STATUS_XON_XOFF and calls the xon/xoff handler with TRUE; class 0x06 (0xE1BA60) clears it, calls with FALSE and advances the output EC.  That reads as 0x05=stop-output(^S) and 0x06=resume(^Q), i.e. the reverse of the current TTY_CHAR_CLASS_XON/XOFF names. close_reason: Resolved from the two default tables plus the handlers. TTY_$I_INIT (0x00E33284) copies the default function characters from 0x00E351D8 (labelled tty_$i_dfl_func_chars); TTY_$I_SET_DFL_FUNCS (0x00E67274) sets A5=0x00E8242C whose first 18 words are the function-index -> char-class table (tty_$i_dfl_func_classes), with the enable mask 0x0001FFFF at 0x00E82450. Function index 13 = char 0x13 (^S, DC3 = XOFF) -> class 0x05; index 14 = char 0x11 (^Q, DC1 = XON) -> class 0x06. That matches the handlers: class 0x05 (0x00E1BA42) bset.b #2,(0x9,A2) and calls the handler with st (TRUE); class 0x06 (0x00E1BA60) bclr.b #2 and calls with clr.w (FALSE) then advances the output EC. tty_$i_put_chars returns 0 while bit 2 is set (0x00E1B032). title: TODO: STOP_$WATCH has two unbounded indices (op >= 8 and parent >= 16)
description: stop/watch.c: (1) the operation branch table at 0x00E81854 has entries only for 2..7 but the guard at 0x00E8183E is 'cmp.w #1 / ble' with no upper bound, so op >= 8 jumps into the middle of instructions; the C default: case does nothing. close_reason: Verified and mirrored.  (1) The operation code has NO upper bound (0x00E8183E is 'cmp.w #1,D3 / ble' and nothing else).  The table's island runs 0x00E81858..0x00E81896, and operation 7's entry is a FOUR-byte bsr.w, so ops 8, 9 and 10 land on real instruction boundaries: 8 -> 0x00E81864 'ori.b #0x81,D6' (a register the exit movem restores) then the common exit, 9 -> 0x00E81866 'move.l D1,(A1)', a long poke that MISSES the DISK_$DIAG gate operation 7 goes through, 10 -> 0x00E81868 the exit branch itself.  All three are now emitted (STOP_OP_ORI_D6 / STOP_OP_POKE_LONG_UNGATED / STOP_OP_NOP in stop/stop.h).  Op 11 lands on the gate at 0x00E8186A entered by jmp not bsr, so its rts returns to the caller with the frame still linked and its refusal path pops the caller's return address; 12+ land mid-instruction -- documented, not reproducible.  (2) The parent slot index is guarded only by 'blt' (0x00E81988).  The scaling is 'lsl.w #6' (wraps mod 0x10000) and the base is reached with a sign-extending 'adda.w' (0x00E81990), and 0x40*0x400 == 0x10000, so the slot number is the low ten bits with 0x200..0x3FF coming out NEGATIVE.  stop/watch.c now computes exactly that. title: SMD_$LOCK_DISPLAY and SMD_$BIT_SET are hand-written asm; move to smd/sau2/
description: SMD_$LOCK_DISPLAY (0x00E15CCE, 68 bytes) has no link/unlk, takes its arguments straight off the stack via (0x4,SP)/(0x8,SP), and brackets its body with ori #0x700,SR / andi #0xf8ff,SR (a forced IPL 0, not an SR restore). title: fp/fp_internal.h FP_SAVE_AREA_BASE 0x00E21928 points into FIM_$BUS_ERR code
description: FP_SAVE_AREA_BASE is defined as 0x00E21928, but that address is inside FIM_$BUS_ERR: it is the extension words of the 'cmpi.b #0xA0,(0x22,%sp)' at 0x00E21926 that distinguishes a 68020 format A frame from a format B one.  It cannot be an FP save area.  The macro is currently unreferenced, so nothing is broken today, but it should be corrected or removed - FIM_$FSAVE (0x00E21C34) and FIM_$FRESTORE (0x00E21CD4) are where the real base can be recovered.
close_reason: FP_SAVE_AREA_BASE removed; the real base recovered. FP_$SAVEP (0x00E218D0) is not a save-pending flag but a LONGWORD POINTER to the per-address-space save-area table: fp_$switch_owner_d2 loads it with movea.l (-0x24c,PC),A1 at 0x00E21B1A (0x00E21B1C-0x24C = 0xE218D0) and fp_$check_owner with movea.l (-0x4ac,PC),A1 at 0x00E21D7A; fp_$save_state (0x00E21B5C) and fp_$restore_state (0x00E21B30) then address a slot as (-0x4,A1,asid*0x14A). The table is allocated at boot by PEB_$LOAD_WCS (move.l A0,(0x00e218d0).l at 0x00E3207C, A0 from the allocator at 0x00E43982) and cleared by OS_$SHUTDOWN (0x00E6D52E); it is 0 in the image, which is what the tst.l in FIM_$FP_ABORT (0x00E21B80) and FIM_$FP_INIT (0x00E21BB0) tests. Confirmed 0x00E21928 is inside FIM_$BUS_ERR. fp_save_area_t re-laid out from the assembly as a packed 0x14A-byte slot whose LAST longword is the frame pointer, with the frame written DOWNWARD (fsave -(A0), then FP0-7 / FPCR-FPSR-FPIAR / the 0xFFFF marker), and given unconditional _Static_asserts; the 326 available bytes are exactly 2+12+96 plus the 216-byte maximum 68882 FSAVE frame. Also re-emitted the whole FP cluster: fp/sau2/fp_context.s replaced the fabricated '68010 has no FPU' stubs with the real code for fp_$switch_owner (0x00E21B10), fp_$switch_owner_d2 (0x00E21B16), fp_$restore_state, fp_$save_state, FP_$GET_FP (0x00E21D48), fp_$check_owner (0x00E21D70) and FP_$PUT_FP (0x00E21D94) - every instruction encoding matches the image bytes read with gsk read (206f/7000/323c, f320/f218 9c00/f218 d0ff/f358/f220 e0ff/f220 bc00/f23c 9000 0000 f400, 2031 28fc, 41f1 08fc, 2388 08fc, 48e7 3000, 4cdf 000c), using the gas (sym:w,%pc) form to reproduce the 4-byte 303a/227a/487a PC-relative operands. fp/get_fp.c and fp/put_fp.c deleted: both omitted the fp_$restore_state / fp_$save_state calls entirely, and neither could express the A1-survives-between-calls contract that makes FP_$GET_FP / FP_$PUT_FP assembly. fp.h and fp_data.c retyped FP_$SAVEP as m68k_ptr_t with the correct description; fim/sau2/fim.s's 'non-zero if FPU hardware is present' comment corrected in place. New fp/test/test_save_area.c (5 tests) checks the 0x14A slot, the state cell at 0x146, the frame budget, the slot arithmetic against the record, the asid-0 skip, and the exact save/restore frame shape. Ghidra: disassembly comments at 0x00E218D0 and 0x00E21928, decompiler comments at 0x00E21B30 and 0x00E21B5C.

title: msg_$data_t layout and its dead inline accessors
description: msg/msg_internal.h's msg_$data_t puts depth[224] at 0x1E, which ends at 0x1DE, yet the ownership bitmaps start at 0x1D8 (0x00E59BFC 'lea (0x1D8,A1),A1') - the depth table cannot be 224 entries at that offset.  Recover the real layout from MSG_$OPENI/MSG_$ALLOCATEI.  Also msg_$check_ownership / msg_$set_ownership / msg_$clear_ownership / msg_$get_depth / msg_$set_depth are unused, ARCH_M68K-only and now duplicate the MSG_$SOCK_OWNERS extern added for MSG_$WAITI; fold or delete them.
close_reason: msg_$data_t recovered from MSG_$OPENI (0x00E591B4), MSG_$ALLOCATEI (0x00E592E6), MSG_$CLOSEI (0x00E593E4) and MSG_$WAITI (0x00E59BC0). The apparent overlap was a one-based array: the ownership base 0x1D8 is the address of slot ZERO of an array indexed by the socket number ('lsl.w #0x3,D2w / lea (0x0,A5,D2w),A0 / lea (0x1d8,A0),A1' at 0x00E59202-0x00E5920A), and socket 0 is impossible - MSG_$OPENI rejects <= 0 at 0x00E591CE and MSG_$CLOSEI at 0x00E593FA - so the lowest bitmap any caller can reach is socket 1 at +0x1E0. The depth table at 0x1E+socket*2 (0x00E59276, 0x00E5936C) therefore ends exactly at 0x1E0. Traced every reference to A6-0x2C in the 1814-byte PROC2_$FORK: writes come only from callees handed 'pea (-0x2c,A6)' at 0x00E72D02 (PROC1_$ALLOC_STACK), 0x00E72D46 (PROC1_$BIND), 0x00E72E60 (EC2_$REGISTER_EC1), 0x00E72EA6 (ACL_$ALLOC_ASID), 0x00E72EB6 (AUDIT_$INHERIT_AUDIT), 0x00E72F0E (FILE_$FORK_LOCK), 0x00E72F4A (MST_$FORK), 0x00E72F6E and 0x00E72FA0 (MST_$GET_VA_INFO), 0x00E730FE (PROC1_$RESUME), plus 'bset.b #0x7,(-0x2c,A6)' at 0x00E731B8; reads are at 0x00E73114 (CRASH_SYSTEM) and 0x00E732D6. The MST_$ALLOC_ASID failure branch is taken at 0x00E72CC6, sets bit 31 of the CALLER's status at 0x00E72CC8, then 'bra.w 0x00E73240' at 0x00E72CCC. Every store listed above lies strictly between 0x00E72CCC and 0x00E73240; the range 0x00E73240..0x00E732D4 contains no reference to A6-0x2C at all; and nothing before 0x00E72CCC touches it (the only frame store in 0x00E72BCE..0x00E72CCC is (-0x20,A6) for TIME_$CLOCK). So 0x00E732D6 'move.l (-0x2c,A6),(A2)' hands the caller the previous frame's leftover and discards the real error. That the author knew the difference is visible at 0x00E72C2E, where the 'table full' exit branches to 0x00E732DA, deliberately past that store. No second Domain/OS build to diff against, so the conclusion is documented in proc2/fork.c (a 30-line note on the 'status' declaration plus a note at the branch), in Ghidra (EOL comments at 0x00E72CCC and 0x00E732D6, decompiler comment at 0x00E72CC6), and covered by proc2/test/test_fork.c::test_alloc_asid_failure_goes_to_entry_teardown, which asserts the branch reaches cleanup_entry (0x00E73240) and not cleanup_locked (0x00E73146) and does not assert the indeterminate status.

CHKSUM_$GET_CHKSUM is hand-written assembly: no link/unlk, it reads its argument at (0x4,SP) and returns the 16-bit sum of 512 words in D0 (movea.l (0x4,SP),A0 / moveq #0 / move.w #0xff,D1 / two add.w (A0)+,D0w / dbf).  Per CLAUDE.md it belongs in chksum/sau2/get_chksum.s with a C-ABI wrapper, and the chksum directory then needs adding to SUBSYSTEMS in the Makefile.  Referenced by TODO(source-cm2w) in chksum/chksum.h -- retarget that TODO at the new bead.
close_reason: CHKSUM_$GET_CHKSUM (0x00E0A314, 20 bytes) emitted as chksum/sau2/get_chksum.s and verified byte-for-byte: m68k-elf-objcopy -O binary gives 206f00047000323c00ffd058d05851c9fffa4e75, identical to the image bytes from gsk read 0x00E0A314 20. It is hand-written asm (no link/unlk, argument read at (0x4,SP), result left in D0). chksum/chksum_internal.h added with CHKSUM_LOOP_COUNT (0xFF, so the dbf body runs 256 times) and CHKSUM_WORDS_PER_ITER; chksum/chksum.h gained CHKSUM_PAGE_WORDS/CHKSUM_PAGE_SIZE and lost its TODO. chksum/get_chksum.c is the !ARCH_M68K model: it assembles each word from its two bytes so the big-endian sum survives on a little-endian host, and keeps the modulo-2^16 wrap that add.w gives. chksum added to SUBSYSTEMS in the Makefile (between cal and dbuf); the m68k build produces an empty chksum/get_chksum.o and the symbol from chksum/sau2/get_chksum.o, and disk/chksum_page.c's reference now resolves. chksum/test/test_get_chksum.c #includes the .c and calls the real function: 6 tests covering the zero page, the 512-word count, reading exactly 1024 bytes (guard bytes past the page ignored, first and last words counted), big-endian word assembly, the add.w wrap (0x8000+0x8000, 0xFFFF+0x0002, 512*0xFFFF), and order independence. title: Identify the AST common-attributes word at +0x14 that FILE_$PRIV_UNLOCK gates its read-lock probe on
description: file/priv_unlock.c reads AST_$GET_COMMON_ATTRIBUTES' output word at +0x14 (0x00E60240 'tst.w (-0x2c,A6)' with the buffer at A6-0x40) and only asks the lock holder for a read lock (REM_FILE_$LOCAL_READ_LOCK) when it is zero. AST_$GET_COMMON_ATTRIBUTES (0x00E04A00) fills it at 0x00E04A46 from the full attribute record's +0x74. The field's meaning is unidentified, so the accessor is spelled FILE_CATTR_W14 in file/priv_unlock.c. Identifying it should also produce a proper struct for the common-attributes record, which several file/ and dir/ call sites currently treat as a raw byte buffer.
close_reason: The word at ast_$common_attr_t+0x14 is the object's REFERENCE COUNT (aote+0x80). Derivation: AST_$GET_COMMON_ATTRIBUTES (0x00E04A00) has 'link.w A6,-0x90' and the whole frame is the full attribute record, so 'move.w (-0x1c,A6),(0x14,A2)' at 0x00E04A46 reads record+0x74 (-0x1C + 0x90); AST_$GET_ATTRIBUTES fills that record verbatim from aote+0x0C ('lea (0xc,A2),A0' + moveq #0x23 + 36 long moves at 0x00E049A2), so record+0x74 = aote+0x80, which is the word AST_$SET_ATTR_DISPATCH's attributes 6/7/8 increment ('addq.w #0x1,(0x80,A2)' at 0x00E04CEE) and decrement (0x00E04D52), both guarded by 'cmpi.w #-0xb' = 0xFFF5 and status_$ast_refcount_underflow. FILE_$PRIV_UNLOCK therefore only asks the lock holder for a read lock when the object has no references left. Produced the struct the bead asked for: ast_$common_attr_t in ast/ast.h (0x18 bytes, offsets asserted) with obj_type/sub_type/attr_flags_hi/attr_flags_lo at 0x00..0x03, length at 0x04 (record+0x14 = aote+0x20), mod_time at 0x08, blocks at 0x10, refcount at 0x14, access_flags at 0x16. Fixed ast/get_common_attributes.c, whose two source offsets were wrong (it read record+0x1C instead of +0x74 for the refcount and record+0x25 instead of +0x65 for the access flags - the A6 displacements had not been rebased by 0x90). Converted every call site off the raw byte buffer: file/priv_unlock.c (now attrs.cattr.refcount / .obj_type), file/set_prot.c, dir/validate_handle.c, dir/do_op_add_mount.c, dir/do_op_create_dir.c, dir/old_set_default_acl.c, dir/do_op_add_bak.c, dir/do_op_add_link.c and log/init.c. Six of those were writing 0x18 bytes into buffers of 1, 4 or 8 bytes; four were reading the wrong offset (add_mount read +0x03 instead of the sub_type at +0x01, add_bak and create_dir read +0x04, log/init read +0x00 instead of the length at +0x04); five were passing a bare uid_t where the callee needs a 0x20-byte file_$obj_loc_t with the UID at +0x08; and dir/do_op_add_bak.c had the sub-type test inverted (0x00E50B24-0x00E50B3C ORs three seq results and 'bmi' takes the DELETE path when one matched, so only sub-types 0/4/5 may be replaced). dir/validate_handle.c's attribute block is now fully wired from the record instead of seven uninitialised locals, including the type-9-process OS-only check at 0x00E4B4B6-0x00E4B4D8 that was missing. title: Revisit CPU architecture vs SAU vs feature-level code organization
description:
The current code organization uses SAU (System Architecture Unit) numbers for platform-specific code splits (e.g., ec/sau2/advance.s). However, this conflates several different concerns:

1. **CPU architecture** (m68k vs x86 vs ARM) - instruction set, calling conventions, register usage
2. **SAU variants** (sau1, sau2, etc.) - Apollo-specific hardware configurations
3. **Feature-level differences** - e.g., MMU type, peripheral support

The ec/sau2/*.s files contain m68k assembly for SR (Status Register) manipulation to disable/enable interrupts. This is fundamentally a CPU architecture concern, not an SAU-level concern - the same code would work on any m68k-based SAU.

Consider reorganizing to something like:
- `ec/arch/m68k/` for m68k-specific assembly
- `ec/arch/x86/` for x86 equivalents (when porting)
- Keep SAU-level splits only for actual hardware variant differences

This would make the retargetability goal clearer and avoid confusion about what each directory level represents.
close_reason: Closed

title: CAL_$WRITE_CALENDAR writes the MSM5832 leap bit at D10 bit 3, TIME_$READ_CAL uses bit 2
description: cal/write_calendar.c 0x00E816D6 does 'add.w #0x50,D1w' on the day before splitting it into tens/ones, which sets bit 3 of the D10 (date tens) register.  TIME_$READ_CAL sets the leap flag with 'bset.l #2' (0x00E2AE78) and masks the date tens with 3 (0x00E2AEC8), i.e. bit 2 - which is where the MSM5832 datasheet puts the leap-year bit.  The 0x50 looks like the 24-hour-select idiom used for the hour (0x00E816EA, H10 bit 3) applied to the wrong register.  Both sides are reproduced faithfully in C with a TODO comment in cal/write_calendar.c; this bead tracks confirming the hardware behaviour (MSM5832 datasheet / a second SAU image) before deciding whether it is an original bug.
close_reason: Confirmed an original bug in the writer; both sides left reproduced as found. MSM5832 D10 (address 8) is {D0,D1 = date tens, D2 = leap year, D3 = unused}; H10 (address 5) is {D0,D1 = hour tens, D2 = PM, D3 = 24-hour select}. Both routines compute the SAME leap predicate -- (year mod 100 + (month > 2)) mod 4 == 0 (writer 0x00E816C0..0x00E816D4; reader 0x00E2AE60..0x00E2AE72, where the -0x51/+0x64 and the +1 cancel the 80) -- but deposit it in different bits. TIME_$READ_CAL uses bset.l #2 (0x00E2AE78) = D10 bit 2 and masks the date tens with 3 (0x00E2AEC8), which is correct. CAL_$WRITE_CALENDAR does add.w #0x50,D1w (0x00E816D6) before the /10 split; since (v+80)/10 == v/10 + 8 and (v+80)%10 == v%10, that lands in D10 bit 3, the unused bit, so the chip's leap counter is never programmed. The identical add.w #0x50 on the hour (0x00E816EA) IS correct because H10 bit 3 is the 24-hour select -- the idiom was copied onto the wrong register. The correct constant for the date would have been 0x28. Benign in practice: the reader masks D10 with 3 and the chip ignores D3, and TIME_$READ_CAL rewrites D10 with bit 2 set on every read taken in a leap year. Documented in cal/cal.h (resolved note + MSM5832_D10_UNUSED), cal/write_calendar.c and time/read_cal.c; cal/test/test_write_calendar.c now asserts D10 bit 3 set and bit 2 clear. Ghidra EOL comments at 0x00E816D6, 0x00E816EA, 0x00E2AE78, 0x00E2AEC8 and a decompiler comment at 0x00E8167C.

title: dxm_entry_t is 24 bytes on the host build, 16 in the image
description: dxm/dxm.h models dxm_entry_t.callback as a native function pointer, so on a 64-bit host the record is 24 bytes and data moves from +0x04 to +0x08.  The image entry is 16 bytes (DXM_$ADD_CALLBACK scales indices with lsl #4 at 0x00E17060 and 0x00E17102, DXM_$SCAN_QUEUE at 0x00E17176), so the _Static_asserts in dxm/dxm.h are ARCH_M68K-only and dxm/test/test_add_callback.c has to lay its entry array out with an explicit 16-byte stride.  Fixing it means making the field a 4-byte cell (m68k_ptr_t) everywhere and unifying the callback cells, which are currently modelled three different ways: m68k_ptr_t in tty/tty_internal.h, void* in term/term.h and ast/ast_internal.h, and a function pointer in suma/suma_internal.h and dxm/dxm_internal.h.  Referenced by a TODO in dxm/dxm.h.
close_reason: dxm_entry_t is now 16 bytes on every target and its _Static_asserts are unconditional. dxm/dxm.h gained dxm_$callback_t (= m68k_ptr_t, the 4-byte code address the image stores at entry+0x00, proved by lsl.l #0x4,D0 at 0x00E17060, lsl.w #0x4,D1w at 0x00E17102 and lsl.w #4,D0w at 0x00E17176), plus dxm_$callback_fn_t, DXM_$CALLBACK_CELL, dxm_$callback_fn and DXM_$DEFINE_CALLBACK_CELL. On m68k those are plain casts; on a 64-bit host DXM_$DEFINE_CALLBACK_CELL registers the function in a table in dxm/dxm_data.c through a constructor (a truncated function address is not a constant expression, confirmed: 'initializer element is not a compile-time constant') and dxm_$callback_fn maps a cell back to a callable pointer. All five cells unified on that type: PTR_TTY_$I_DXM_SIGNAL (tty/tty_internal.h + tty_data.c), PTR_TERM_$ENQUEUE_TPAD_00e1ce90 (term/term.h + term_data.c), PTR_AST_$SET_TROUBLE_00e07272 (ast/ast_internal.h), PTR_TERM_$ENQUEUE_TPAD_00e1aecc (suma/suma_internal.h), PTR_DXM_$ADD_SIGNAL_CALLBACK (dxm/dxm_internal.h + dxm_data.c); tty/term/ast gained the dxm/dxm.h include, and the two stale (void **) casts on the callback argument (dxm/add_signal.c, suma/rcv.c) were dropped. DXM_$ADD_CALLBACK's callback parameter is now const dxm_$callback_t *; add_callback.c and scan_queue.c updated. dxm/test/test_add_callback.c dropped its explicit 16-byte-stride byte block and its two slots of slack for a plain dxm_entry_t[8], and uses literal code addresses for the callbacks (the function only compares and stores the cell). New dxm/test/test_scan_queue.c #includes dxm/dxm_data.c and dxm/scan_queue.c and drives the real DXM_$SCAN_QUEUE: 5 tests covering the 16-byte record, the host registry round trip, the empty queue, draining in head order with the head advanced and the lock dropped before each callback, and the masked head wrap. Ghidra: disassembly comments at 0x00E17060 and 0x00E17176. Follow-up source-f4qo filed for the two cells that still have no definition anywhere.

title: SMD_$START_BLT is hand-written assembly; move to smd/sau2/
description: SMD_$START_BLT's implementation at 0x00E15D1E has the same shape as SMD_$LOCK_DISPLAY: no link/unlk, a movem thunk, arguments read straight off the stack at (0x8,SP)/(0xc,SP)/(0x10,SP), register-passed dispatch base in A0, and a trampoline at 0x00E272BC (lea (-0x39e,PC),A0 / jmp).  Per CLAUDE.md it belongs in smd/sau2/start_blt.s with a portable C model under !ARCH_M68K, the way smd/sau2/lock_display.s and smd/sau2/bit_set.s were done under source-c3ap.  smd/start_blt.c is still plain C.
close_reason: Transcribed to smd/sau2/start_blt.s.  Confirmed hand-written: the entry at 0x00E272BC is 'lea (-0x39e,PC),A0' + 'jmp 0x00e15d1e.l', and the body at 0x00E15D1E has no link/unlk, saves exactly one register with 'movem.l {A2},-(SP)', reads its three arguments at (0x8,SP)/(0xc,SP)/(0x10,SP) with the movem push folded into the displacements by hand, and ends in a spin on a memory-mapped register ('tst.w (A1)' / 'bmi.b' at 0x00E15D80/0x00E15D82).  Behaviour: seven parameter words copied in the order 1,3,2,4,5,6,7 (0x00E15D2E-0x00E15D52); the control word is params[0] & 0xFFDE | hw->video_flags (0x00E15D58-0x00E15D5E); if bit 4 is set it presets hw->lock_state = 1, clears the whole word at hw+0x20 and copies hw->op_ec.value into hw->field_1c (0x00E15D68-0x00E15D72) and returns after starting the BLT, otherwise it spins.  Verified with m68k-elf-gcc -c + m68k-elf-objdump -d: the 108-byte body is byte for byte identical to 0x00E15D1E..0x00E15D89 - the one instruction GNU as would have normalised, 'and.w #-0x22,%d0' (0xC07C vs ANDI's 0x0240), is emitted with .short so nothing differs.  The trampoline keeps the original's shape and length (0x41FA + 0x4EF9, 10 bytes) but its lea displacement cannot be reproduced until SMD_$DISP1_INT (0x00E26F20) is emitted - filed as source-tzn8 with a TODO in the file; A0 is dead anyway, overwritten at 0x00E15D22.  smd/start_blt.c is kept as a portable model behind '#if !defined(ARCH_M68K)', the same convention as bit_set.c and lock_display.c.  Ghidra: decompiler comment at 0x00E15D1E.
